title: Origin and evolution of the genetic code: the universal enigma
funder: The authors' research is supported by the Department of Health and Human Services intramural program (NIH, National Library of Medicine).
authorConflicts: No statement in the PMC author manuscript.
result: Review. The standard genetic code maps 64 codons, each a triplet of nucleotides, to 20 amino acids and two punctuation marks, start and stop signals; 61 codons code for amino acids and three are stop codons; the code is shared, with relatively minor modifications, by all known life forms. Selenocysteine and pyrrolysine are encoded by special schemes in subsets of organisms.
